items.t: Fungal skin infections (dermatophytes, moulds, yeasts including Candida), skin disease with secondary fungal infection, and candidal nappy rash, vulvitis and balanitis.

src.q: All dermatomycoses due to moulds and other fungi
All dermatomycoses due to yeasts

items.t: All fungal skin infections; particularly suited to hairy skin and to fungal infections of the outer ear (otitis externa) and middle ear (otomycosis).

src.q: should be used to treat all fungal skin infections due to dermatophytes, yeasts, moulds and other fungi
It is particularly suitable for use on hairy skin and in fungal infections of the outer ear (otitis externa) and middle ear (otomycoses).

items.t: Candidal vaginitis (vaginal thrush).

src.q: are recommended for the treatment of candidal vaginitis
Clotrimazole vaginal tablets are indicated for the treatment of candidal vaginitis.

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction stated in the five UK SmPCs accessed (cream, solution, 100 mg pessary, 500 mg pessary, 500 mg vaginal tablet) or the BUMPS leaflet.

items.t: Cream: apply thinly 2 to 3 times daily and rub in gently. Continue for at least 1 month for dermatophyte infections and at least 2 weeks for candidal infections.

src.q: The cream should be applied thinly 2-3 times daily and rubbed in gently.
Treatment should be continued for at least one month for dermatophyte infections and at least two weeks for candidal infections.

items.t: Solution: apply thinly and evenly 2 or 3 times a day and rub in gently. Continue for at least 2 weeks after all signs of infection have gone.

src.q: should be thinly and evenly applied to the affected area 2 or 3 times a day and gently rubbed in
treatment should be continued for at least two weeks after the disappearance of all signs of infection

items.t: Adults: two 100 mg pessaries daily (preferably at night) for 3 days, or one 100 mg pessary daily for 6 days. A second course may be given if needed.

src.q: Two pessaries should be inserted daily (preferably at night) for three consecutive days.
Alternatively, one pessary may be inserted daily for six days, preferably at night.
A second treatment may be carried out if necessary.

items.t: Adults: one 500 mg pessary or vaginal tablet inserted at night as a single dose. A second treatment may be given if needed.

src.q: One 500mg pessary should be inserted at night.
The treatment consists of one vaginal tablet to be inserted at night, using the applicator provided.
A second treatment may be carried out if necessary.

items.t: Cream and solution: no separate dose schedule for children (same use as adults).

src.q: There is no separate dosage schedule for the young or elderly.
There is no separate dosage schedule for the elderly or the young.

items.t: 100 mg pessary and 500 mg vaginal tablet: not for use in children under 16 years.

src.q: Not for use in children under 16.

items.t: Vaginal forms: medical advice is needed before use if this is the first episode, more than two episodes in 6 months, past sexually transmitted disease or exposure to a partner with one, pregnancy or suspected pregnancy, age under 16 or over 60, or known hypersensitivity to imidazoles or other vaginal antifungals.

src.q: Medical advice should be sought if this is the first time the patient has experienced symptoms of candidal vaginitis.
more than two infections of candidal vaginitis in the last six months
previous history of a sexually transmitted disease or exposure to partner with sexually transmitted disease
pregnancy or suspected pregnancy
aged under 16 or over 60 years

items.t: Vaginal forms: do not use, and seek medical advice, if there is irregular or abnormal vaginal bleeding or blood-stained discharge, vulval or vaginal ulcers, blisters or sores, lower abdominal pain or painful urination, fever or chills, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, or foul-smelling discharge.

src.q: should not be used if the patient has any of the following symptoms whereupon medical advice should be sought
abnormal vaginal bleeding or a blood-stained discharge

lower abdominal pain or dysuria
fever or chills
foul smelling vaginal discharge

items.t: Vaginal forms: if symptoms are not relieved within 1 week, or thrush recurs more than twice in 6 months, the patient should see a doctor.

src.q: Patients should be advised to consult their physician if the symptoms have not been relieved within one week
if the candidal infection recurs more than twice within six months, patients should be advised to consult their physician

items.t: Cream: contains cetostearyl alcohol (may cause local skin reactions) and benzyl alcohol (may cause allergic reactions and mild irritation). Fabric that has been in contact with the cream burns more easily and is a serious fire hazard: no smoking or naked flames.

src.q: This product contains cetostearyl alcohol, which may cause local skin reactions (e.g. contact dermatitis).
The cream also contains benzyl alcohol which may cause allergic reactions and mild local irritation.
Instruct patients not to smoke or go near naked flames - risk of severe burns.
Fabric (clothing, bedding, dressings etc) that has been in contact with this product burns more easily and is a serious fire hazard.

items.t: Latex condoms and diaphragms: the product may damage latex and reduce contraceptive effect. Use other precautions during use and for at least 5 days after.

src.q: this product may cause damage to latex contraceptives
Patients should be advised to use alternative precautions for at least five days after using this product.
this product may cause damage to latex contraceptives

items.t: Vaginal clotrimazole with oral tacrolimus or sirolimus: levels of these may rise; monitor closely for overdose signs, with plasma levels if needed.

src.q: Concomitant treatment with vaginal clotrimazole and oral tacrolimus (FK-506; immunosuppressant) might lead to increased tacrolimus plasma levels and similarly with sirolimus.
Patients should thus be closely monitored for signs and symptoms of tacrolimus or sirolimus overdosage

items.t: Solution in the ear: a heat reaction has been reported when used together with a named combination ear drop product.

src.q: There have been reports of a heat reaction when Canesten Solution is used concomitantly with Sofradex drops in the ear.

items.t: Can be used in pregnancy, but only under the supervision of a doctor or midwife. Harmful effects are not expected at the low systemic exposure.

src.q: Clotrimazole can be used during pregnancy, but only under the supervision of a physician or midwife.

src.q: During pregnancy the pessary should be inserted without using an applicator.

items.t: BUMPS: clotrimazole can be used in pregnancy and is the first-choice treatment for thrush; no known risks.

src.q: Clotrimazole can be used in pregnancy and is the first-choice treatment for thrush.

items.t: May be used during breastfeeding; systemic absorption is minimal. If cream or solution is used on the nipple area, wash the breasts before feeding.

items.t: Frequencies are not known (spontaneous reports). Skin forms: redness, itching, rash, stinging or burning, blistering, peeling, contact dermatitis, application-site irritation or pain.

blister, dermatitis contact, erythema, paraesthesia, skin exfoliation, pruritus, rash, urticaria, stinging skin/burning sensation skin

src.q: vaginal exfoliation, vaginal discharge, vaginal haemorrhage, vulvovaginal discomfort, vulvovaginal erythema, vulvovaginal burning sensation, vulvovaginal pruritus, vulvovaginal pain

items.t: Vaginal forms: insert as high as possible into the vagina with the applicator, ideally at bedtime lying on the back with legs bent. The product needs vaginal moisture to dissolve.

src.q: The pessaries should be inserted into the vagina, as high as possible, using the applicator provided.
This is best achieved when lying back with legs bent up.

items.t: Vaginal forms: do not use during the menstrual period; finish treatment before the period starts.

src.q: Treatment during the menstrual period should not be performed due to the risk of the pessary being washed out by the menstrual flow.

items.t: Cream on the feet: wash and dry the feet, especially between the toes, before applying.

src.q: If the feet are infected they should be washed and dried, especially between the toes, before applying the cream.

items.t: Vaginal forms: do not use tampons, douches, spermicides or other vaginal products during treatment; avoid vaginal intercourse, as the partner could become infected.

src.q: Do not use tampons, intravaginal douches, spermicides or other vaginal products while using this product.
Vaginal intercourse should be avoided in case of vaginal infection and while using this product because the partner could become infected.
